label: v3-opus-high
prompt:
You are reviewing pull request #${{ github.event.pull_request.number }} as a code reviewer.
The PR's head is checked out in the working directory. Its diff against the base
branch is in ${{ runner.temp }}/pr.diff; read it first. Then read every file the diff
touches in full, and the unchanged code it calls or is called by: a bug often lies in
how the change interacts with code it doesn't touch. Follow the repository's own
conventions (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, docs/ and .github/instructions/ where present).

Your review may be the only one this PR gets before it merges on its own, so be
thorough. For each change, ask what happens on the paths the author didn't test:
another event or trigger, a rerun, a skipped or cancelled job, a different actor
(a bot, an app, a person without write access), an empty, malformed or unusual
input (whitespace, tabs, Unicode, markup), a race between two runs. For GitHub
Actions workflows and merge gates, reason about how GitHub itself behaves: which
events fire, what a skipped or failed check does to a PR's mergeStateStatus, who
the actor is, what each token can do. Where the behaviour of a pinned action or of
GitHub decides the answer, read its source or documentation rather than guess.
Look hardest at code that decides whether something merges, releases or gets
permissions, and at text processing that turns input into rendered output.

Report every real problem a maintainer would want fixed or knowingly accepted
before merging: bugs, security issues, broken edge cases, missing or wrong tests,
and clear departures from the repository's conventions. Don't report style nits,
praise, or the PR's scope (what it bundles together is the author's call).

Every finding names a file path relative to the repository root and a line number
on the new side of that file, on a line the diff adds or shows as context: a finding
anywhere else holds the merge until the next push. When the problem lies in code the
diff doesn't touch, put the finding on the changed line that calls it, depends on it
or should have changed with it. Before you report a line, read it in the checked-out
file (not in the diff) and make sure it is the line the finding is about. Say what
goes wrong, in which situation, and how to fix it.

Answer with a short summary of the change and your verdict, and your findings.

review.summary: This PR adds a label-triggered "Claude Review" workflow as a backup to Copilot. A read-only review job produces JSON findings, and a post job turns them into a github-actions[bot] review whose body starts with `<!-- claude-review -->`. PR Auto-Merge accepts that review of the head like Copilot's, counts Claude rounds toward the shared cap, and skips unresolved Claude threads at the cap. The PR also collapses marker spacing in release-post commit subjects, drops `ready_for_review` from CI, and times out a hung Playwright install. Verdict: request changes. Any PR can fake the review that unlocks auto-merge, because PR-controlled code (the PR's own workflow and post script) can post a marked github-actions[bot] review. The release_post change also brings back the empty-list-item bug for subjects with a leading tab. Other findings: off-diff findings block the merge even after the review cap; a label added by a triage-only person can block the merge (likely, not confirmed); and docs/PROCESS.md still describes the old gate. I checked all of this by reading the code; I couldn't run the tests or the workflow.

findings.body:
**Any PR can fake a Claude review that unlocks auto-merge.** Auto-merge treats any github-actions[bot] review whose body starts with the marker as a review of the head. Claude Review runs on `pull_request`, so it uses the PR's own copy of `claude-review.yml`, and the post job (claude-review.yml:135-150) checks out the PR's `.github/scripts/post_claude_review.py` and runs it with `pull-requests: write`. Any same-repo PR can also add a new workflow that posts as github-actions[bot] with the marker.

Failure case: a PR (for example one written by Sandcastle) edits the post script to always post `<!-- claude-review -->\nNo findings.`, or adds its own workflow that does. Auto-merge then sees a review of the head and merges with no real review. This weakens the rule this file states for itself ("a PR can't edit the script that decides whether it merges"); Copilot's review can't be faked this way.

Fix: post the review from a workflow that always runs main's copy. For example, have the review job upload the findings as an artifact and post them from a `workflow_run`-triggered workflow that checks out main. Alternatively, have PR Auto-Merge confirm that the Claude Review run that posted the review came from main's workflow file.

**Regression: a commit subject with a leading tab can render as an empty list item again.** The leading-whitespace skip changed from `lstrip(" \t")` to `lstrip(" ")`, so a leading tab is no longer skipped when there is no container marker (`after == 0`).

Failure case: the subject `<!--x-->\t[a]: x` is sanitized to `\t[a]: x`. `after_containers` returns 0, `start` stays 0, and `DEFINITION_LIKE_SUBJECT.match` fails on the tab, so nothing is escaped. The output is ``- \t[a]: x (`abc1234`)``. GitHub (cmark-gfm) reads the item's content as the reference definition `[a]: x` with the title ``(`abc1234`)``, so the list item renders empty. Before this PR, `lstrip(" \t")` caught this case.

Fix: use `.lstrip(" \t")` here, and add the test case `("<!--x-->\t[a]: x", "\t\\[a]: x")`.

**Findings outside the diff block the merge even after the review cap.** When any finding lands outside the diff, this exit fails the Claude Review check. A failing check, even a non-required one, makes `mergeStateStatus` UNSTABLE, and PR Auto-Merge only merges CLEAN. The cap in pr-automerge.yml is meant to stop reviewers holding the merge, but this check isn't covered by it.

Failure case: a PR past the 3-round cap still has `review:claude`, so every push gets a new Claude review. Each review with a finding outside the diff fails the check and blocks the merge again, so the PR can chase reviews indefinitely.

Fix: once the cap is reached, don't fail the step. Either pass the cap state to the script or compute it in the post job, or have the script skip the `sys.exit(1)` at the cap. Add a test for that case.

**Adding the label can block the merge instead of starting a review (likely, not confirmed).** The `if` filters out bots only, but as far as I know `claude-code-action` also refuses any actor without write permission. I couldn't read the pinned action's source to confirm this.

Failure case: the header says a person can add `review:claude` at any time. If a person with only triage access adds it, the Review step would fail. The failed check makes the PR UNSTABLE until the next push, which blocks the merge. An expired `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, an API outage or the 15-minute timeout has the same effect on every labelled PR.

Fix: either check the actor's permission in the `if` (or in a first step that skips the review), or set `continue-on-error` on the Review step and have the post job skip when there is no output.

**docs/PROCESS.md still describes the old merge gate.** The gate now accepts a Claude review of the head, and the cap counts Copilot and Claude rounds together. But docs/PROCESS.md:64-67, the process standard AGENTS.md points to, still says auto-merge waits until "Copilot has reviewed its latest commit" and stops after "three Copilot review rounds". Update it in this PR, including how and when `review:claude` is used.

review.summary:
This PR adds Claude Review as a backup reviewer for when Copilot doesn't review. It's opt-in through the `review:claude` label. A read-only job has Claude review the diff and return JSON findings, and a second job posts them through `post_claude_review.py` as one COMMENT review under github-actions[bot]. The review body starts with `<!-- claude-review -->`. PR Auto-Merge now accepts that review in place of Copilot's and counts both reviewers toward one shared cap of review rounds. Findings that fall outside the diff hold the merge in two ways: a second marker line in the review body, and a failing post job. The PR also tidies how `release_post.py` handles quote and list markers at the start of commit subjects (this part looks correct and is tested), stops running CI on `ready_for_review`, and adds a 10-minute timeout to the Playwright install.

Verdict: don't merge yet. The gate now trusts any github-actions[bot] review whose body starts with the marker, and the PR's own copy of the workflow posts it. So code inside a PR can write the review that lets that PR merge. Second, the failing post job makes the review cap stop applying to findings outside the diff. Third, findings that use absolute paths, which Claude Code's tools produce, will be treated as outside the diff and hold the merge. Finally, `docs/PROCESS.md` still describes a gate that only Copilot can satisfy.

findings.body:
**Code inside a PR can forge the review that lets it merge.** PR Auto-Merge counts any github-actions[bot] review whose body starts with `<!-- claude-review -->` as a review of the head. github-actions[bot] is the `GITHUB_TOKEN` identity, and any `pull_request` workflow with `pull-requests: write` can post as it.

Those workflows run the PR's own copy of the file. `claude-review.yml` is one of them, and its post job (claude-review.yml:138-141) checks out the PR's merge ref, so it also runs the PR's own `post_claude_review.py`. `ci.yml`'s docs-label job is another.

A same-repo PR can therefore edit `claude-review.yml` or `post_claude_review.py`, or add a workflow step, to post `<!-- claude-review -->\nNo findings.` on its own head. PR Auto-Merge then treats the PR as reviewed and squash-merges it once checks are green. A Sandcastle PR could do this without anyone noticing.

This undoes the guarantee the rest of this file is built on: it uses `pull_request_target` "so a PR can't edit the script that decides whether it merges". Copilot's review couldn't be forged this way; this one can.

**Fix:** post the review under an identity PR code can't use. For example, a GitHub App or PAT token kept in an environment secret limited to `main`, used only by a workflow that runs main's copy of the workflow (`workflow_run` or `pull_request_target`, taking the findings from an artifact). Then match that login here instead of github-actions[bot] plus a marker.

**The deliberate `sys.exit(1)` stops the review cap from applying to findings outside the diff.** The failed "Post Claude's review" check sets the head's `mergeStateStatus` to `UNSTABLE`, and PR Auto-Merge only merges when it is `CLEAN`. So the off-diff bypass at pr-automerge.yml:309/344 ("merging past Claude's findings outside the diff") can't actually merge.

The test `merges past off-diff findings at the review cap and says so` (pr-automerge.test.mjs:539) only passes because it uses `mergeStateStatus: "CLEAN"`. A real head in that state would be `UNSTABLE`.

While the label is on, every push after the cap gets a new Claude review. Each one that again puts a finding outside the diff fails the check again. A PR can therefore chase Claude's findings outside the diff with no limit, which is what the cap exists to prevent.

The outcome also depends on something unrelated: someone adding any label on the same head starts a skipped run that replaces the failed check (the docstring acknowledges this), and then the cap bypass works.

The `OFF_DIFF_MARKER` already holds the merge below the cap. **Fix:** report the findings outside the diff as a warning or job summary and exit 0, so the cap behaves the same for threads and for findings outside the diff.

**`path` is used exactly as Claude returns it, so absolute or `./`-prefixed paths count as outside the diff.** Claude Code's Read/Glob/Grep tools work with absolute paths, such as `/home/runner/work/Articles/Articles/src/x.cs`, so the model will often report findings that way, or as `./src/x.cs`.

No such key exists in `diff_lines()`, so every such finding lands in the review body. The check fails, and the merge is held until the next push, even when the finding sits on a changed line.

**Fix:** normalize the path before the lookup. Strip a leading `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/` (pass it in, or use `os.path.relpath` against the workspace when the path is absolute), then `os.path.normpath` and drop any leading `./`. Add a test for each form.

**The process doc wasn't updated.** The merge gate now accepts a Claude review of the head and counts Copilot's and Claude's rounds together toward the cap.

`docs/PROCESS.md:64-67`, which AGENTS.md makes the source of truth for merging, still says PR Auto-Merge merges once "Copilot has reviewed its latest commit" and stops waiting "after three Copilot review rounds". It doesn't mention `review:claude`, Claude Review's threads, or how findings outside the diff hold the merge.

People and agents following the doc will misread why a PR merged or why it's held. **Fix:** update that section in this PR.

review.summary: Adds a Claude Review workflow (claude-review.yml + post_claude_review.py) as a Copilot backup and teaches PR Auto-Merge to accept a github-actions[bot] review whose body starts with <!-- claude-review --> as a review of the head. Copilot and Claude rounds share the review cap, and a second marker holds the merge when a finding sits off the diff. It also drops ready_for_review from CI, adds a 10-minute timeout to the Playwright install, and collapses the spaces after list/quote markers in release_post.py commit subjects. The release_post.py change, the GraphQL changes and the cap/thread arithmetic look correct. Verdict: hold for two merge-gate problems. (1) The review that now satisfies the merge gate can be produced by the PR's own code, since it is authenticated only by login plus marker and is posted from the PR's copy of the workflow. (2) Any Claude Review failure or same-head cancellation leaves a failing check that blocks PR Auto-Merge even at the cap. Smaller issues: off-diff findings render badly, and docs/PROCESS.md is stale.

findings.body:
**The PR's own code can produce the review that lets it merge.**

A Claude review is recognised only by author `github-actions[bot]` plus a body starting with `<!-- claude-review -->`. But `claude-review.yml` runs on `pull_request`, so it executes the PR branch's copy of the workflow and of `post_claude_review.py`. Any other `pull_request` workflow can also post a review with a `pull-requests: write` GITHUB_TOKEN.

**Failure case:** a same-repo PR (an agent-written Sandcastle PR, say) edits the prompt, the post script, or adds a workflow step that posts `<!-- claude-review -->\nNo findings.` on its head. PR Auto-Merge then counts it as a reviewer's review of the head and merges.

**Why it matters:** until now that gate needed Copilot, which a PR can't fake. This undoes the design stated at lines 32-34 ("a PR can't edit the script that decides whether it merges").

**Fix:** post the review under an identity PR code can't use, such as a GitHub App or PAT token available only to a job running main's copy (`pull_request_target`/`workflow_run`), and match on that login instead of github-actions[bot] + marker. Alternatively, have PR Auto-Merge confirm a successful run of main's Claude Review workflow for that head SHA.

**Multi-line off-diff findings render badly in the review body.**

Each finding is written as `- `path:line`: {body}` with no indentation for later lines.

**Failure case:** Claude's finding bodies are often multi-paragraph Markdown. After a blank line, the next paragraph, code fence or heading leaves the list item, so the rest of the body and the following findings render as stray top-level blocks. An unclosed ``` in one finding swallows everything after it. A backtick in `path` also breaks the code span.

**Fix:** indent continuation lines so they stay inside the item, e.g. `body.replace("\n", "\n  ")`, and escape the path or use `<code>` for it. Add a test with a multi-paragraph body.

**`docs/PROCESS.md` still describes Copilot-only merging.**

This changes when PR Auto-Merge merges: a Claude review of the head counts, Copilot and Claude rounds share the cap, Claude threads are bypassed at the cap, and off-diff findings hold the merge. But `docs/PROCESS.md:64-67`, which AGENTS.md names as the process reference, still says the PR merges once "Copilot has reviewed its latest commit" and counts "three Copilot review rounds".

**Fix:** update that section, and document the `review:claude` label and the off-diff hold.
